title: House Republicans Elect Jim Jordan to Lead Minority; Thune Re-elected in Senate
dek: House Republicans chose Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan over Majority Leader Steve Scalise after the midterm losses, while Senate Republicans kept John Thune as leader.
author: Meridian Newsroom
keyPoints: House Republicans elected Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio as minority leader for the next Congress on Tuesday, defeating Majority Leader Steve Scalise 106-73 in a secret ballot, two Republican lawmakers told NBC News.
Jordan, 62, chairs the House Judiciary Committee and previously chaired the Oversight Committee.
Senate Republicans re-elected John Thune of South Dakota, who will become minority leader rather than majority leader in January, the Washington Post reported.
NBC News reported that the midterm results gave Democrats roughly 260 House seats, the largest majority in 35 years.
body:
House Republicans on Tuesday chose Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio to lead their conference in the next Congress, [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/republicans-reeling-election-choose-leadership-congress-rcna608300) reported, after the party’s midterm losses.

## House vote

Jordan defeated Majority Leader Steve Scalise of Louisiana, a close ally of outgoing Speaker Mike Johnson, in a secret-ballot vote held behind closed doors, NBC said, citing two Republican lawmakers in the room. The vote was 106-73, the lawmakers said.

“Over the next two years, House Republicans will fight for American families,” Jordan told reporters. “When Democrats offer more government, we’ll offer more freedom, and we will bring that fight in committee, on the floor and on the stump every single day.”

NBC described the result as a signal that House Republicans wanted a clean break from the Johnson leadership team after the midterms. Jordan had told colleagues that his time chairing the Oversight Committee would help him respond to the investigations Democrats have promised into the Trump administration.

## Senate leadership

[The Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/11/10/house-republicans-elect-jim-jordan-serve-minority-leader-next-year/) reported that Senate Republicans kept Thune as their leader. NBC said a small group of conservatives had pushed to delay the Senate leadership election, and that Republicans re-elected their current slate anyway.

## Context

NBC reported that Democrats gained roughly 260 House seats, the largest majority in 35 years, and that Democrats are expected to pursue a series of investigations once Congress convenes under their control. Democrats take control of the House in January.

## Jordan’s background

NBC News reported that Jordan, 62, has spent two decades in Congress. He led the Republican Study Committee, the largest conservative caucus on Capitol Hill, and helped form the House Freedom Caucus, a smaller and more conservative group. In 2018, after Republicans lost the House majority, he challenged Kevin McCarthy for minority leader and lost, 159-43, NBC said.

NBC described Jordan as a fervent supporter of President Donald Trump. It also reported that he had become more of a team player in recent years while leading House committees, and that his ascent came after he pitched colleagues on his experience chairing Oversight to counter the investigations Democrats have promised.

## What comes next

NBC reported that Democrats, who gained roughly 260 House seats in the midterms, the largest majority in 35 years, are feeling “very empowered” as they prepare to take control of the House in January. The Republican leadership votes set the party’s posture for the next Congress, in which it will be in the minority in both chambers. Thune will lead Senate Republicans as minority leader, the Washington Post reported.
